Revision History

Changes from version 1.6 to 1.7

This version mostly adds a bunch of things we needed to enable running Piff on Roman Space Telescope images using an optical model based on the galSim.roman PSF model. The new PSF type is called RomanOptics. See the RomanOpticsPSF docstring for details about the new type. You can also see some example configurations that use it in the devel/roman directory.

Dependency Changes

  • Added pyarrow dependency for reading Parquet input catalogs. It is only required if you attempt to read a parquet file. (#188)

  • Removed support for Python 3.8, 3.9.

  • Added support for Python 3.14, 3.15.

API Changes

  • Deprecated input.nstars in favor of select.nstars, which now works across all input files. The old option is deprecated and retains the per-image behavior. (#190)

  • Renamed select.max_snr to select.max_snr_weight to clarify that this caps a star’s effective fitting weight, rather than rejecting bright stars. The old name is still works but is deprecated. (#195)

  • Deprecated the use of strings to mean FITS-header keywords for noise, gain, satur and sky in the input section. You should now use the new ImageHeaderValue type instead. (#207)

  • Various minor signature changes to Python functions. If you are using the Python interface rather than config files, you may need to check the doc strings for changes to return values or parameter names.

Output file changes

  • Added the number of fitting iterations, niter, to the saved fit diagnostics. (#196)

  • Added the observing bandpass when one is supplied. (#194)

  • Star SEDs are saved as file names and reconstruction metadata, rather than embedding the full spectra. If you do something that needs the SEDs after reading the psf from a file, those SED files must be accessible. (#194, #198)

  • Renamed the WCS table’s nchunks column to wcs_nchunks. Files with the old name should continue to work properly. (#198)

New features

  • Added input.badpix_zeros to mask zero-valued science pixels. (#185)

  • Added support for reading the noise variance from the FITS header. (#186)

  • Added an option to compute the sky level from the median of the input image. Use input.sky: median. (#187)

  • Added support for Parquet input catalogs, using pyarrow. (#188)

  • Added the ability to read multiple image HDUs from a single FITS file to be processed as separate images. (#189)

  • Changed nstars to mean the total number of stars to use across all input images when there are more than one, rather than each image separately. Also moved this to select where it fits more naturally. (#190)

  • Added raw_snr attribute for stars to keep track of their real snr, rather than the possibly adjusted value in snr due to select.max_snr_weight. (#190)

  • Added the ability to compute star properties derived from one or more columns in the input catalog. (#191)

  • Added Centroid outlier rejection with a max_offset threshold, and allow outliers to be a list combining multiple rejection criteria. (#192)

  • Added select.min_sep to reject objects with a nearby neighbor. (#193)

  • Added input.bandpass for specifying the bandpass used for the observations. (#194)

  • Added support stellar SEDs in the input field for chromatic fitting. You can either specify a single spectrum to use for all stars (using input.sed_file_name) or specify a specific spectrum for each star separately (using input.sed_col). There are additional parameters that can control how these files are used. See docs for InputFiles for more details. (#194, #198)

  • Added the RomanOpticsPSF class, based on GalSim’s Roman optical model, with fitted Zernike aberrations and Gaussian priors. (#195, #196, #197, #198)

  • Changed StarImages plots to include chip number and image coordinates for each star. (#196)

  • Expanded support for GalSim-style config value types in the config file, including Eval and Current expressions and their $ and @ shortcuts. (#207)

Bug fixes

  • Ensure input stamps use floating-point data, so sky subtraction and other processing work with integer-valued source images. (#187)

  • Fixed composite PSF serialization when components have parameter-variance arrays of different sizes. (#195)

  • Reject failed HSM measurements when using hsm_size_reject or max_pixel_cut. (#196)

  • Fixed StarImages when fewer eligible stars are available than requested. (#196)

  • Fixed GSObject fitting to avoid nonpositive sizes. (#200)

  • Added checks for excessively large FFTs when fitting and reject them rather than risking huge memory allocations or crashes. (#205)

  • Fixed the TwoDHist model-size panel, which previously repeated the measured star sizes instead of showing model sizes. (#205)

  • Added warning about zero-S/N candidates when no min_snr cut is set, with an additional suggestion to supply noise information when it is missing. (#200)

  • Fixed chi-squared outlier rejection for already-flagged stars. (#208)
